warnings.message: Topic has no hard prerequisites and is not marked foundational.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Powers of i cycle
node.description: Use the repeating cycle of powers of i to simplify expressions involving integer powers of the imaginary unit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Simplify negative square roots with i
node.description: Rewrite square roots of negative real numbers using the imaginary unit and real square-root factors.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Complex equality by components
node.description: Use equality of real parts and imaginary parts to solve simple equations involving complex numbers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Pure real and pure imaginary complex numbers
node.description: Recognise complex numbers with zero imaginary part or zero real part as pure real or pure imaginary cases.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Complex plane axes
node.description: Interpret the horizontal axis as the real axis and the vertical axis as the imaginary axis in the complex plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vector view of complex numbers
node.description: Represent a complex number as a position vector from the origin in the complex plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conjugate reflection in real axis
node.description: Interpret the conjugate of a complex number as reflection across the real axis in the complex plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Modulus formula from Pythagoras
node.description: Calculate the modulus of a complex number using the Pythagorean distance formula from its rectangular components.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Principal argument
node.description: Identify a standard principal argument for a complex number within the chosen argument interval.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Argument quadrant adjustment
node.description: Adjust a reference angle to the correct quadrant when finding the argument of a complex number.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Cis notation
node.description: Use cis notation as shorthand for cosine theta plus i sine theta in polar form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rectangular to polar components
node.description: Convert from rectangular form to polar form by calculating modulus and argument from real and imaginary components.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Polar to rectangular components
node.description: Convert from polar form to rectangular form using cosine and sine components.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Polar multiplication geometry
node.description: Interpret multiplication in polar form as multiplying moduli and adding arguments geometrically.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Polar division geometry
node.description: Interpret division in polar form as dividing moduli and subtracting arguments geometrically.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: De Moivre integer powers
node.description: Use De Moivre theorem to raise a complex number in polar form to a positive integer power.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nth roots argument spacing
node.description: Find all nth roots by spacing their arguments equally around the complex plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Roots of unity introduction
node.description: Find and interpret complex roots of one as equally spaced points on the unit circle.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Negative discriminant gives complex roots
node.description: Use a negative quadratic discriminant to identify and calculate non-real complex roots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conjugate root theorem
node.description: Use the fact that non-real roots of real-coefficient polynomials occur in conjugate pairs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Powers of i repeat every four
node.description: Integer powers of i repeat in a four-term cycle: i, negative one, negative i, one.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Complex equality matches components
node.description: Two complex numbers in rectangular form are equal when their real parts match and their imaginary parts match.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conjugate reflects across real axis
node.description: Taking the conjugate keeps the real part fixed and changes the sign of the imaginary part, reflecting the point across the real axis.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nth roots are equally spaced
node.description: The nth complex roots of a nonzero complex number have arguments separated by equal angles around the complex plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Negative discriminant gives nonreal roots
node.description: A quadratic with real coefficients and negative discriminant has two non-real complex conjugate roots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: i power cycle reset error
node.description: Learner simplifies powers of i by treating every fourth power incorrectly or restarting the cycle at the wrong place.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Complex equality as single equation
node.description: Learner treats equality of complex numbers as one equation instead of matching real and imaginary components separately.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conjugate changes real part
node.description: Learner changes the sign of the real part rather than the imaginary part when finding a conjugate.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Only one nth root found
node.description: Learner finds only the principal root and misses the remaining equally spaced complex roots.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Negative discriminant means no roots
node.description: Learner interprets a negative discriminant as no roots rather than no real roots and two non-real complex roots.

edge.rationale: Simplifying powers of i directly practises the defining behaviour of the imaginary unit.
Matching real and imaginary components directly practises rectangular-form structure.
Principal-argument work is a standard part of interpreting arguments in the complex plane.
Equally spaced arguments are central to finding all complex roots.
Conjugate-pair reasoning is central to complex roots of real-coefficient polynomials.
Simplifying powers of i depends on knowing that i squared equals negative one.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats i as an ordinary variable rather than cycling through powers.

edge.rationale: Rewriting negative square roots uses the definition of the imaginary unit.
edge.failure_signal: Learner leaves negative square roots as real values or mishandles the i factor.

edge.rationale: Component-wise equality depends on identifying real and imaginary parts in rectangular form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sets whole expressions equal without matching components separately.

edge.rationale: Reading complex-plane axes depends on interpreting real and imaginary components.
edge.failure_signal: Learner swaps the real and imaginary axes.

edge.rationale: The vector view builds on plotting complex numbers on the plane.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots a point but cannot interpret it as displacement from the origin.

edge.rationale: Reflection interpretation of conjugates requires the complex-plane representation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reflects across the imaginary axis or changes the wrong component.

edge.rationale: The modulus formula follows from distance from the origin in the complex plane.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds components directly instead of using squared distances.

edge.rationale: Quadrant adjustment builds on understanding argument as direction angle.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses the reference angle without checking the quadrant.

edge.rationale: Choosing a principal argument requires correct quadrant-adjusted arguments first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives a coterminal angle outside the chosen principal interval.

edge.rationale: Cis notation is shorthand for trigonometric polar form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats cis as a separate function rather than cosine plus i sine notation.

edge.rationale: Rectangular-to-polar conversion requires calculating modulus and argument.
edge.failure_signal: Learner computes magnitude but uses an unadjusted reference angle.

edge.rationale: Polar-to-rectangular conversion uses the cosine and sine components of polar or cis notation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner swaps sine and cosine components or omits the i on the imaginary part.

edge.rationale: Geometric multiplication interpretation depends on representing complex numbers in polar form.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds moduli or multiplies arguments instead of multiplying moduli and adding arguments.

edge.rationale: Polar division is the inverse operation to polar multiplication, using modulus division and argument subtraction.
edge.failure_signal: Learner subtracts moduli or divides arguments.

edge.rationale: De Moivre powers generalise repeated polar multiplication.
edge.failure_signal: Learner powers the modulus but fails to multiply the argument by the exponent.

edge.rationale: Finding nth roots uses polar powers and argument periodicity from De Moivre reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds only one root or spaces arguments unevenly.

edge.rationale: Roots of unity are a special case of equally spaced nth roots on the unit circle.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not include all roots around the circle.

edge.rationale: Interpreting negative discriminants occurs within solving quadratics with complex roots.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports no roots instead of no real roots.

edge.rationale: Conjugate-pair reasoning is first visible in quadratic equations with real coefficients.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses one non-real root without including its conjugate in a real-coefficient polynomial.
